questions.question: How can a driver prevent a rollover?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo low.
questions.explanation: Vehicles roll over when turned too quickly. Keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible. This prevents rollovers.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.
Assists with the operation of brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, what should the trailer height be?

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, where should the landing gear be?
questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly on the ground.
questions.explanation: When uncoupling a trailer, lower the landing gear until it touches the ground firmly. If the trailer is loaded, turn the crank a few more times to remove some weight from the trailer.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a trailer jackknife?
questions.correctAnswerText: Continue the skid.
questions.explanation: If the trailer is jackknifing, release the brakes to help the tires regain traction. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: Are fully-loaded rigs more or less likely to roll over than empty rigs?

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes too quickly?

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect, resulting in a rollover.
Confusion over which lane the driver is hoping to use.
Other drivers to reduce their speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect, resulting in a rollover.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle causes a "crack-the-whip" effect. This can result in a rollover.

questions.question: What is the best way to tell if your trailer is skidding?

options.text: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has left the lane.
Release the brake pedal and then push it down again.
Watch the jackknife warning light on the control panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has left the lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a trailer skid. Check your mirrors anytime you brake hard to make sure your trailer is in its proper lane.

questions.question: What should you do if your trailer goes off course while backing?

options.text: Continue the backing process without changing anything.
Pull the truck forward, readjust, and start backing again.
Get out of the truck and move the trailer into the right position.
Turn the steering wheel all the way to the left until the trailer straightens out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull the truck forward, readjust, and start backing again.
questions.explanation: If your trailer goes off course while backing, pull the truck forward. Reposition your vehicle as needed and then continue backing.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether a pre-1998 trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), how can you check?

options.text: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes. This tells you if the trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your vehicle's air tanks, the brakes:
questions.correctAnswerText: May not work correctly.
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil buildup. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Large combination vehicles take the longest amount of time to stop when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Empty.
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. With less weight, the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, the driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. This allows the wheels to regain grip on the road. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Are easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. They require more driving skill.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand valve while driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen.
A valve that prevents the driver from going too fast.
A valve that prevents the trailer from accidentally being released.

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?

options.text: It is a square blue knob.
It is a triangular yellow knob.
It is an eight-sided red knob.
It is a circular orange knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is an eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob on newer vehicles. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, you should not:

options.text: Allow the wheels to grip the road.
Allow the trailer to straighten out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels grip the road again. Do not apply the trailer hand brake. Using brakes is what locked the wheels in the first place and caused the skid.

questions.question: If colors are used to identify glad hands, which color is used for emergency lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: When trailer air lines are color-coded, service lines are blue and emergency lines are red.

questions.question: Test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Removing the parking brake control knob.
Releasing air with the brake pedal.
Releasing air with the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air supply charge, turning off the engine, then pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.
